trust_decision.summary: The post-login redirect target must resolve to a same-origin absolute path: SkyServer.Redirect prepends '/', strips leading slashes, parses, and requires an empty Host and Scheme before issuing the 307, but it never decodes percent-escapes first, so an encoded '//' normalises to a protocol-relative Location after the browser decodes it.

landing_point.why: It is the only origin check in the login flow and the first place an engineer who read 'login flow open redirect' would land; the fix adds one condition to this same line.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /sky/callback (skyserver.go:159) and GET /sky/login with a valid auth cookie (skyserver.go:98) both call SkyServer.Redirect

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exist; the nearest dismissal a solver could attempt is treating the legacy /login forwarder as unvalidated because skymarshal/legacyserver/server.go:21-23 says validation is deliberately delegated to the newer paths, but that forwarder passes the query into the same checked sink.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate percent-encoded path content must survive: '/teams/main/pipelines/my%20pipeline' must still redirect to that pipeline path, and the legacy fly flow's encoded query separator 'redirect_uri=/fly_success%3Ffly_port=<port>' must still work; a fix that rejects any '%', or unescapes and then re-appends csrf_token without noticing the new query, changes what the fly client receives.

O6_input_shapes: encoding nested more than 5 times (rejected with 400)
legitimate %20 space in a pipeline path (must be preserved)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A legacy /login handler that resolves the redirect target itself instead of forwarding the raw query to /sky/login
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already hand-rolls the legacy auth redirects, already builds a redirect_uri from the fly_port parameter, and its comment relegates validation elsewhere, so a maintainer adding the old-path passthrough there is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Normalising the redirect_uri in NewLogin before it is signed into the state token, instead of at the sink
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The state token is the natural place to sanitise a value that has to survive a round trip through the IdP, and a maintainer could reasonably put the check where the value is produced rather than where it is used.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A tlsRedirectHandler variant that redirects to a caller-supplied external host or path prefix
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already composes a Location from request-derived Scheme/Host/Path/RawQuery, which is exactly the shape a redirect-target check would guard.

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.26.3 (go.mod:3), modules only, no vendor directory
O10_build.project_tests: Ginkgo v2 suite skymarshal/skyserver/skyserver_test.go driven by TestSkyServer in skymarshal/skyserver/skyserver_suite_test.go:32; it runs entirely in-process with httptest plus a gomega ghttp TLS server as the fake IdP (skyserver_suite_test.go:45-79), so no external service or network is needed. Existing cases already assert that a literal '//example.com' state value returns 404 (skyserver_test.go:460-469).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Unescape the redirect_uri once (url.QueryUnescape) before the existing TrimLeft plus Host/Scheme check: it fixes the report's single-encoded %2F example and still misses the double- and triple-encoded state values.

out_of_scope_notes: skymarshal/legacyserver/server.go:34-48 builds a Location from r.URL.Host (the Host header) with an empty Scheme, a host-header-driven redirect shape that is not the redirect_uri protection this advisory covers; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb: could not measure the checkout size (no shell in this session); source is clearly well over 5 MB but that is an estimate, so no tiny_repo/giant_repo flag was raised.

O7: the state token round trip (JSON plus base64 RawURL, skyserver.go:243-297) is lossless for the redirect_uri string, so the serialization boundary does not itself move the cause out of the sink; j_cause_other_layer is therefore 0 even though a producer is recorded.
Whether either target model actually fails on this host: not testable from the tree, and the single-sink shape suggests it would not.
